column1: # Forbric kernel -- Minecraft-line rename table for 1.21.1
# The runtime source set (src/runtime/java) is written in the 26.2 namespace. A second Minecraft line gets
# the table below applied at build time, because every entry here is a MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE name: it exists on
# one line and does not exist on the other. Re-measure, do not trust this sentence:
# So no single spelling compiles on both lines, and a blanket rename in the sources is not available. Each
# entry below was checked in BOTH directions against the staged merged bases
# and, where a member is involved, against the method signature with `javap`.
# Format: <26.2 name> TAB <1.21.1 name>   ('#' starts a comment; blank lines ignored)
# Rules are applied longest-first and whole-token only ((?<![A-Za-z0-9_$]) ... (?![A-Za-z0-9_$])), so
# `Identifier` never reaches inside `KernelIdentifier` and a fully-qualified rule always wins over its own
# simple name. The build FAILS if a rule matches nothing, so a table entry that has gone stale is an error
# Mojang renamed ResourceLocation -> Identifier in 26.x. Same class, same members: parse, tryParse,
# tryBuild, fromNamespaceAndPath, withDefaultNamespace, getNamespace, getPath all exist on both sides
# A member rename, not a class rename. 26.2 ResourceKey has `Identifier identifier()` and no `location()`;
# 1.21.1 ResourceKey has `ResourceLocation location()` and no `identifier()` (javap both). 17 call sites,
# all on a ResourceKey. TagKey#location() already has this name on BOTH lines, so it is left alone -- the
# rule rewrites `identifier()`, which TagKey never had.
# Renamed to MobSpawnType. Verified through the method that consumes it: 1.21.1
# MobSpawnType.SPAWNER / NATURAL / MOB_SUMMONED / TRIGGERED / TRIAL_SPAWNER all exist.
# 26.2 split the entity constants (EntityTypes) from the registry type (EntityType); 1.21.1 has both on
# EntityType, whose ZOMBIE / DROWNED / ZOMBIE_VILLAGER / SKELETON / SPIDER are public static finals. A
# whole-token rule, so `EntityType` written already -- which the sources never do -- would be untouched.
# net.minecraft.world.entity.vehicle.Boat (1.21.1). 1.21.1's `Boat` is what the type is for -- it carries
# the paddle constants and is the common base of the boat family.
# 26.2 moved three entity classes into their own subpackages; 1.21.1 keeps them flat. Simple names unchanged.
# 26.2 split the particle registry/reload-listener (ParticleResources) away from the ticking engine
# (ParticleEngine); 1.21.1 has the two roles on ParticleEngine, which is the class that implements
# PreparableReloadListener and owns the `providers` map the kernel reads on both lines. Role-based mapping,
# which is why it is written down: it is the one entry here that is not a literal rename.
# DELIBERATELY ABSENT -- measured as absent from 1.21.1 and NOT a rename. These need the code restructured,
# which changes 26.2 too, so they are not table entries. Adding one of them here makes the build compile and
#   net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.FuelValues     fuel values are a furnce-block-entity concern
#   net.minecraft.server.packs.metadata.pack.PackFormat   pack format is an int before 1.21.9
#   net.minecraft.client.gui.Hud                          the HUD is Gui/GuiGraphics before 26.x
#   net.minecraft.client.gui.render.pip.*                 picture-in-picture renderers do not exist pre-26.x
#   net.minecraft.util.random.WeightedList                API differs, not a name: 1.21.1 has no Builder
# MEMBER-level counterparts checked with javap and NOT expressed as rules, because each one changes the shape
# of the expression rather than a name. Kept here so the next agent does not have to re-derive them:
#       1.21.1 has no PackFormat at all, and the consumer differs too: 26.2 builds
#       PackMetadataSection(Component, InclusiveRange<PackFormat>) while 1.21.1 takes an int pack format.
#       KernelClientPackSource needs a real branch, not a substitution.
#   Gui.overlay() / Gui.hud                (26.2) -> no counterpart: 1.21.1 has no Gui/Hud split
#   Minecraft.gui.setScreen/screen()/disconnectWithSavingScreen would be ten clean renames, but they are
#   EXPRESSION fragments (`gui.` disappears), so they are deliberately not rules: this file maps names, and
#   mixing in expression rewrites would make it mean two different things. Their containing files are blocked
